reveal.summary: Dolly Parton. The butterfly is her lifelong symbol. The misty mountains are Locust Ridge, Tennessee, where she grew up one of twelve children in a one-room cabin. 9 to 5 is her film, her song, her Oscar nomination — played on her acrylic nails. 'I Will Always Love You' is hers too: written in 1974, and she turned down Elvis rather than give up half the publishing, which is why Whitney's 1992 recording made her a fortune. In 2020 she quietly gave $1 million to the Vanderbilt fund that helped develop the Moderna vaccine. Her Imagination Library has mailed more than 200 million free books to children, in honor of a father who never learned to read. And since 1986, her name has been on the gate of a theme park in those same Smokies.
reveal.evidenceToAnswer: The board narrows honestly: the butterfly keeps everyone alive; the Smokies clear Canada and Oklahoma but spare both Appalachians; 9 to 5's year retires Taylor; the quote tempts you to tap Whitney — the one move that loses — until spring 2020 makes her impossible; the book program separates the two women from the hollers; and only one suspect owns a theme park in those mountains.
